findings.source_quote: τήρει οὖν τὴν ἁγνείαν καὶ τὴν σεμνότητα, καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.
findings.english_quote: So keep purity and reverence, and you will live to God.
findings.issue: “Reverence” shifts σεμνότητα from dignified moral seriousness in one's conduct to an attitude of profound respect or veneration. The lexical metadata correctly identifies dignified moral seriousness, but that explanation does not make the main-text word communicate the same quality. This is a semantic substitution, not merely a preference for a different register.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, consider: “So keep purity and dignity, and you will live to God.” Alternatively, consider “purity and dignified seriousness” if “dignity” alone would obscure the ethical sense. Align the lexical rationale and footnote with whichever wording is subsequently approved.

findings.source_quote: τήρει οὖν τὴν ἁγνείαν καὶ τὴν σεμνότητα, καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.
findings.english_quote: Keep purity and reverence, and you will live to God.
findings.issue: Independently against the Greek, “reverence” presents an attitude of respect or veneration rather than the dignified moral seriousness expressed by σεμνότητα here. The simplified edition's metadata explains the intended meaning, but the reader-facing wording still substitutes a different quality.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, consider: “Keep purity and dignity, and you will live to God.” Another candidate is “Keep purity and seriousness in your conduct, and you will live to God.” Review the latter for its explanatory expansion before adopting it, and update the corresponding metadata.

summary: Both editions preserve the two historical sections, the difficult repentance–forgiveness distinction, the selected positive reading in III.6, the one-repentance assertion, both remarriage permissions, and the stated conditions for forgiveness. Reader-facing “servants” and contextual “repentance” comply with current policy. The disclosed variants do not warrant replacing the working reading. The supplied reports support the notes' bounded distinction between reported readings, editorial restoration, and preserved text; this review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. One localized semantic correction is proposed in each edition; replacement wording requires fresh review.
